results.title: AI Use-Case Compass — Retail & E-Commerce
results.content: # **AI Use-Case Compass — Retail & E-Commerce: Personalization at Planet Scale**. **Artificial intelligence (AI)** is transforming the retail and e-commerce industry at an unprecedented pace, promising improved efficiency, customer experiences, and growth across virtually every sector. **Generative AI** — AI that creates new content (text, images, designs, etc.) — and **agentic AI** — autonomous decision-making systems or agents (including robots and AI assistants) — are now being applied alongside traditional AI analytics in retail. A 2024 industry survey found that 42% of retailers (and 64% of large retailers) already use some form of AI, and nearly half believe **generative AI** will be a market differentiator [1], [2]. Analysts have projected **$240-$390 billion in annual value for the retail sector** from **generative AI** alone, equivalent to a 1.2–1.9 percentage point increase in profit margins [3]. Major retailers like **Walmart** have declared they are “all-in” on AI, embedding generative and agentic tools across workflows in 2024–25 [4].

results.title: The role of decision rules and network effects over time
results.content: # From platform growth to platform scaling: The role of decision rules and network effects over time. Platform business need to combine indirect and data network effects to transition from growth to scaling. Using an inductive theory elaboration approach with a longitudinal case study of a two-sided platform, Takeaway.com, we offer in-depth understanding about how the top management team members used decision rules to navigate emergent opportunities and challenges over time, and to transition from platform growth to platform scaling. We find that the top management team members purposefully and repeatedly use and revise a portfolio of decision rules to cultivate indirect and data network effects, which allows them to initially facilitate the growth of their platform and over time support the transition to scaling the platform. Our findings provide important implications about the distinct nature of platform growth and platform scaling, and the role of decision rules in cultivating a combination of network effects over time in order to arrive at platform scaling and ensure platform survival and prosperity over an extended period.
